title: Social Work Fields of Service
description: Fields of services in which social workers perform professional roles. Focus on social work approach to intervention in practice and policy arenas.

title: Introduction to Social Work and Social Welfare
description: Orientation to field of social work. Develop understanding of social work principles, goals, values, and methods through readings and class discussion. An unpaid assignment in an agency setting is required. Scheduling is flexible.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Cultural Pluralism
description: Understanding of the American society as a culturally pluralistic social process and an understanding of social work as a culturally directed profession with emphasis on the concept of cultural identities created by one’s values, ideologies, knowledge and behavior.

title: Perspectives on Human Behavior and the Social Environment
description: Interdisciplinary, comparative, and critical approach to explanatory theories of human behavior. Focus on interrelatedness of factors that affect the nature and quality of human life with linkage to the social welfare of individuals, families and communities.

title: Human Behavior Across the Life Span
description: Psycho-social, biological, cultural and environmental influences on individual growth and development and how knowledge is utilized by social work generalist practitioners in assessment and intervention.

title: Social Policies and Social Issues
description: Major social forces and institutions as they relate to and determine social policy emphasizing social welfare services in an industrialized society.

title: Practice Skills Micro
description: Micro skills utilizing motivational interviewing within overall generalist practice framework. Written and verbal communication, interviewing, and assessment with individuals.

title: Practice Skills Macro
description: Development of social work practice skills at macro level. Written and verbal communication needs assessment and resource development with organizations and communities.

title: Methods of Social Work Research
description: Definition and purpose of research in social welfare and social work. Formulation of research problems, selecting a design and methodology; techniques of collecting, organizing, interpreting, and analyzing data.

title: Social Work Practice: Child Welfare
description: Problems of children and supportive, supplementary and substitute social services which have been developed to meet these needs.

title: Social Work Practice: Family Issues
description: Issues relative to social work intervention with families, including major social work and interpersonal family problem situations. Family practice methods and social service provisions, and social policy issues around family needs.

title: Alcohol and Other Drug Problems: Prevention and Intervention
description: Alcohol and other drug issues related to individuals, groups, and society. Concepts include preventive methods, secondary prevention, self-help groups, models of treatment, prevention strategies in communities, and overview of alcohol and drug policies.

title: Generalist Social Work Practice I
description: Integration of social work theory, principles, and practice techniques across micro and mezzo social work populations to include families and groups.

title: Generalist Social Work Practice II
description: Integration of social work theory, principles, and practices with emphasis on mezzo and macro generalist practice social work populations and settings.

title: Field Experience in Social Work
description: A minimum of eight units (four in Social Work 489A and four in

title: Field Experience in Social Work
description: A minimum of eight units (four in

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Investigation and Report
description: Analysis of special topics in social welfare.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Social Work in Healthcare Settings
description: Study of social work in healthcare integrating theory, principles, and social work practice. Topics include treatment modalities, theoretical approaches, levels of practice, specific client groups, and/or specialty areas.

title: Seminar in Loss and Grief Theories and Practice
description: Multidisciplinary perspectives on bereavement, death, and dying through ethical, legal, medical, psychological, and spiritual lenses. Cultural diversity, direct practice, life span development.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics in social work.

title: Seminar in Social Welfare Policy and Services
description: Social welfare as a social institution; philosophical, historical, and comparative analysis of the welfare functions, issues and problems in both policy and program development, implementation, and evaluation.

title: Computer Application in Practice for Social Work and Gerontology
description: Computer technology in social work practice with emphasis on clinical and administrative applications, program monitoring, and support of service provision and delivery.

title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment
description: Conceptual framework to view and interpret behavior and to understand functioning of individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities within ecological systems.

title: Seminar in Human Behavior and Social Environment: Direct Practice
description: Human behavior theories and concepts appropriate to a methods concentration.

title: Social Work Practice: A Generalist Perspective
description: Overview of generalist social work practice as a method and process. Generalist social work presented as a basic helping approach used to assist individuals, groups, families, organizations, and communities to achieve personal and social change.

title: Social Work Practice: Individuals, Families, and Groups
description: Preparation for direct intervention with individuals, families, and groups.

title: Social Work and Gerontology: Organizations and Communities
description: Theoretical knowledge of elementary organizational and interorganizational decision making in human service programs.

title: Field Practicum
description: Field instruction in public or voluntary social work setting. Seven units required. Experiences emphasize application of social work objectives, principles, and skills in service to individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities.

title: Social Work Foundation Practice Skills
description: Skill development and application of social work practice. Engagement, assessment, risk assessment, application of theoretical models to client interventions.

title: Generalist Foundation of Social Work Practice, Policy, and Human Behavior
description: Reviews generalist foundation of social work curriculum. Practice concepts at all practice levels, human development theories, and social welfare policies.

title: Seminar in Research Methods for Social Work and Gerontology
description: Research development, design, and methodology. Application to social work and gerontology in testing theories, advancing practice knowledge, and decision-making.

title: Seminar on Selected Topics
description: Intensive study in specific areas of social work.

title: Seminar in Selected Social Welfare Policy and Services
description: Selected social welfare policies used to examine processes of policy formulation, policy analysis skills, and relationships of policy decisions and indecisions to outcomes of social welfare interventions.

title: Seminar in Selected Topics in Human Behavior and Social Environment
description: Selected topics related to current theories of natural and induced change in human behavior which have utility for social work practice within fields of service.

title: Advanced Seminar in Social Work Practice with Families
description: Family dynamics and social work practice related to family change.

title: Advanced Seminar in Administration and Community Development in Social Work and Gerontology
description: Human services program design, strategic planning, marketing, organizational performance management, human resource management, and development of grant proposals.

title: Advanced Seminar in Selected Topics in Direct Practice Social Work
description: Study of a selected aspect of direct practice social work. Topics include treatment methodology, theoretical approaches, levels of practice, specific client groups, or special problem areas.

title: Advanced Seminar in Selected Topics in Social Work Administration
description: Study of selected aspects of administration in human services organizations to include leadership, organizational learning, organizational change management, and supervision.

title: Advanced Field Practicum: Direct Practice Social Work
description: Advanced field instruction in public or voluntary social work setting. Eight units required. Continuation and intensification of experiences in application of social work objectives, principles and skills in service to individuals, families, groups and communities.

title: Advanced Field Practicum: Social Work Administration and Community Development
description: Advanced field instruction in public or voluntary social work setting. Eight units required. Continuation and intensification of experiences in application of social work objectives, principles and skills in service organizations and communities.

title: Seminar in Social Work and Selected Fields of Practice
description: Traditional and emerging fields of practice and related social work responsibilities and roles.

title: Seminar in Social Work and Selected Populations-at-Risk
description: Social work practice with selected populations-at-risk such as one-parent families, children in institutions, ethnic minority immigrants, Native-Americans in the urban scene, and foreign-born brides of U.S. servicemen.

title: Seminar on Selected Populations-at-Risk
description: Knowledge about and analysis of selected populations-at-risk, social work responsibilities in emerging service demands by diverse and needful, high risk segments of the population in a complex society, and implications for social work practice. Population- at-risk for study to be announced in Class Schedule.

title: Applied Social Work Practice Research Seminar
description: Preparation for practitioner-researcher role through application of social work research concepts and procedures in practice situations (in class and field) of social work interventions.

title: Research
description: Research in one of the areas of social work.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.

title: Seminar in Etiology and Pharmacology of Substance Abuse
description: Advanced seminar experience related to alcohol and other drug etiological models and epidemiology of substance abuse.

title: Seminar in Global Approaches to Substance Abuse Prevention and Treatment
description: Current science related prevention and treatment of substance misuse. Cultural and societal aspects of substance abuse treatment.

title: Seminar in Theoretical Approaches to Substance Abuse
description: Social science theory as it relates to substance use and misuse. Classic and current theory from ecological approach related to extant science.

title: Advanced Seminar in Substance Abuse Research
description: Substance abuse to include randomized clinical trials, prevention trials, field research, mixed methods, epidemiological approaches, etiological research. Classic methodological texts and emerging approaches examined.

title: Advanced Multivariate Data Analysis
description: Substance use and misuse to include analyses of biomarkers, complex survey data, observational data, and multi-level data.

title: Doctoral Research
description: Prior to advancement to candidacy; Independent investigation including the general field of the dissertation.

title: Doctoral Dissertation
description: Preparation of the dissertation for the doctoral degree. Enrollment is required during the term in which the dissertation is approved.
